data.one_liner: MongoDB driver implemented in pure Dart for server-side applications.
data.what_it_does: Provides a server-side MongoDB driver written in pure Dart. It supports all CRUD operations, aggregation pipelines, authentication methods, and secure TLS/SSL connections.
use_when: You are building a Dart or Flutter server-side application that needs to connect to MongoDB.
You require full CRUD operations, aggregation pipelines, and change streams in pure Dart.
avoid_when: You need client-side database storage inside a mobile app (use local NoSQL/SQL solutions instead).
You are relying on deprecated legacy commands for very old MongoDB versions without migration.
strengths: Implemented in pure Dart with no external native dependencies.
Supports modern MongoDB protocol operations (OP_MSG), bulk writes, and aggregation pipelines.
Compatible with cloud services like MongoDB Atlas and Azure DocumentDB.
weaknesses: Not suitable for client-side mobile storage directly due to server-side architectural design.
Porting of all modern MongoDB commands is still a work in progress.
data.setup_notes: Add mongo_dart to your dependencies and initialize a Db connection string.
